<description>
This is just me finding a few more edge cases after #34156 and #34176

The goal of the PR is to handle failures in a controlled way. Just so the process can automatically restore the original wallet without requiring user manual intervention.

The covered cases are:

1. During `DoMigration()`: There are methods that can throw exceptions and abruptly abort the process.
Instead of crashing (GUI) or returning a generic exception, we now will catch and return the error gracefully. This lets the process restore the original wallet automatically.

2. Trying to migrate a wallet in a read-only directory throws a filesystem exception and skips cleanup.
 Now the process will fail gracefully with a clear error msg, and automatically restore the original wallet.

3. Any failure during `MigrateToSQLite` requires user manual intervention.
Now the original wallet db will remain untouched, and only be updated once the sqlite db creation fully succeeds.
</description>

[2026-11-05] rc:4481335276 inline on src/wallet/wallet.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-05):
In commit "wallet: migration, make sqlite creation robust against failures" (b9486540d774f2e07ecce93af0637d6e685a93e0)

Would it work to create the temporary database next to the original file, in `origin_db_path.parent_path()`, instead of in the wallets directory? Then it is always on the same filesystem as the destination, and the `copy_file` call below could be a `fs::rename`:

- The move becomes atomic, so a failure can't leave a partially copied `wallet.dat` behind.
- There is no need to copy a possibly large file, or for the new `copy_file` overload in `fs.h`.
- As far as I can tell `copy_file` doesn't sync the new file to disk before `remove_tmp()` deletes the source, so a crash shortly after migration could leave a truncated `wallet.dat`. A rename keeps the data sqlite already synced.

For directory wallets that location is the wallet's own directory, and for plain-file wallets it's the directory containing the file, where the new wallet directory is created. The read-only directory test would then fail earlier, when creating the temporary database, with a different message, which seems fine since nothing has been changed at that point either. The other-filesystem test would still be worth keeping.
[2026-11-05] rc:4481335289 inline on src/wallet/wallet.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-05):
In commit "wallet: migration, make sqlite creation robust against failures" (b9486540d774f2e07ecce93af0637d6e685a93e0)

Here and in the `fs::remove(origin_db_path)` error case below, `fail()` removes the temporary files while `new_db` still has the database open. I believe on Windows the removes fail (and the errors are ignored), leaving the `_sqlite_*.tmp` directory behind, and on other platforms sqlite keeps writing to an unlinked file until `new_db` is destroyed. Could call `new_db.reset();` before both `return fail(...)` calls, or declare `new_db` before the `fail` lambda and reset it there.

Also, `remove_tmp` only deletes the data file, so a `wallet.dat-journal` left by a failed commit or rollback would keep the directory from being removed. It could delete everything in `new_db->Files()`, saved before the reset.

Thanks, this is much better now that all records are written before the original file is removed, and the catch added in the last commit covers `TryCreateDirectories` throwing. But from reading the code I think two failures after this `fs::remove` still need manual recovery:

- If `copy_file` fails, `fail()` deletes the temporary sqlite db and `MigrateToSQLite` returns false. `MigrateLegacyToDescriptor` then [returns the error right away](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/3ca388f099c6a161faa40bf8b91c5aa89cb5b11d/src/wallet/wallet.cpp#L4324) without reaching the [restore code](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/3ca388f099c6a161faa40bf8b91c5aa89cb5b11d/src/wallet/wallet.cpp#L4413-L4462), so the wallet directory is left with no `wallet.dat` (or possibly a partial one), and the only copy of the wallet is the `.legacy.bak` file, which the error message doesn't mention.
- If reopening the database fails, the `Assert` on `MakeDatabase` crashes the node.

One way to cover both would be to throw instead of returning false once the original file is removed, and the same instead of the `Assert`, so the new catch block sends them through the restore path. Returning false is still right before that point, since the original file is untouched then. The [separate comment](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34193#discussion_r4481335276) about renaming instead of copying would also remove the partial copy case.

[2026-11-05] rc:4483885369 inline on src/wallet/wallet.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-05):
In commit "wallet: use RunWithinTxn within MigrateToSQlite" (038d663391621f14e2dcb08ce1a6d9296646689e)

Using `RunWithinTxn` here is nice: it makes the write loop much easier to follow and puts the begin, write and commit failures in one place. But this commit is hard to review because it isn't a refactoring, it changes how failures are handled, and the next commit replaces that failure handling again. I think the simplest fix is to restructure the commits; otherwise there are a few problems to fix here.

**Suggested restructuring:** keep only the `walletdb.cpp`/`walletdb.h` part in this commit, which is a real refactoring, and move the `MigrateToSQLite` change into the next commit "wallet: migration, make sqlite creation robust against failures" (b9486540d774f2e07ecce93af0637d6e685a93e0). That commit rewrites this block anyway, so its diff would then go directly from the old asserts to the new error returns, and the cleanup problems below would be covered by [the comment on `fail()`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34193#discussion_r4481335289). Commit message for this commit could be:

```
wallet: add RunWithinTxn overload taking a DatabaseBatch

Refactoring, no behavior change. Make the static RunWithinTxn helper a template so it works with both WalletBatch and DatabaseBatch, and add a WalletDatabase overload whose callback takes a DatabaseBatch. The next commit uses it in MigrateToSQLite to write the migrated records in one transaction and return an error if that fails.
```

**If you keep this commit as it is**, these should be fixed:

1. The database is no longer closed before its file is deleted, and only `wallet.dat` is deleted. Deleting the data file of an open database can leave `wallet.dat-journal` behind as a [hot journal](https://www.sqlite.org/howtocorrupt.html#_mispairing_database_files_and_hot_journals_), and since the new database is created at the wallet's own path, SQLite could roll it back into a new `wallet.dat` created there later, for example when the migration is retried after restoring the backup.

2. `fs::remove` is the throwing overload. If it throws (likely on Windows, which can't delete an open file), the exception skips the `assert(false)` that is meant to stop the node, and at this commit nothing in the migration catches it, so the RPC returns an error and the node keeps running.

3. `assert(false)` normally means a programming bug, but here runtime errors (full disk, I/O error, corrupt database) reach it, which isn't obvious to readers.

Something like this would fix all three:

```cpp
if (!written) {
    // Can be reached by runtime errors such as a full disk, an I/O error or a corrupt database.
    const std::vector<fs::path> files{new_db->Files()};
    new_db->Close();
    for (const fs::path& file : files) {
        std::error_code ec;
        fs::remove(file, ec);
    }
    assert(false); // This is a critical error, the new db could not be written to. The original db exists as a backup, but we should not continue execution.
}
```

4. The commit message should say this isn't a pure refactoring, and that the next commit replaces these asserts. For example:

```
wallet: use RunWithinTxn within MigrateToSQLite

Write the migrated records with RunWithinTxn so failures to begin, write or commit the transaction are handled in one place. The next commit uses this to return an error instead of asserting.

This is a refactoring except on failure paths that still end in assert(false): the new database is now closed and deleted when the transaction can't be started or committed, not only when a write fails, and the failure is logged.
```
[2026-11-05] rc:4484088024 inline on src/wallet/wallet.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-05):
In commit "wallet: migration, make sqlite creation robust against failures" (b9486540d774f2e07ecce93af0637d6e685a93e0)

This can corrupt the migrated wallet if a stale sqlite journal is in the wallet directory. The `copy_file` below puts a complete database at `wallet.dat`, and if a `wallet.dat-journal` from an earlier crashed sqlite write is already there (for example from a migration that crashed in an older version, after the user restored the backup manually), SQLite treats it as a hot journal for the new file and rolls it back into it when `MakeDatabase` reopens it. This happens after the original file is deleted. Master doesn't have this problem because it creates the database in place as an empty file, and SQLite ignores the journal for an empty file.

I checked this with a Python sqlite3 script using the same locking mode as the wallet: 3 of 3 runs corrupted the copied database, twice as "database disk image is malformed" and once silently, passing `integrity_check` with different contents.

It should be easy to fix by failing before the original is removed if the journal exists:

```cpp
// Wallets that are plain files rather than wallet directories will be migrated to be wallet directories.
const fs::path dst_wallet_dir = fsbridge::AbsPathJoin(GetWalletDir(), fs::PathFromString(m_name));

// A journal left at the destination by an earlier crashed sqlite write would be
// rolled back into the new database when it is opened, corrupting it.
const fs::path dst_journal{fs::PathFromString(fs::PathToString(SQLiteDataFile(dst_wallet_dir)) + "-journal")};
if (std::error_code ec; fs::exists(fs::symlink_status(dst_journal, ec))) {
    return fail(strprintf(_("Error: Unable to migrate wallet '%s' because a leftover database journal file exists at '%s'. Move it out of the wallet directory and try again."), GetName(), fs::PathToString(dst_journal)));
}
```

with the later `dst_wallet_dir` declaration removed. A test could be similar to `test_unwritable_dir_failure`: write a dummy `wallet.dat-journal` into the wallet directory, check that `migratewallet` fails with this error, and check the wallet is still BDB.
